analysis.title: Quality bonds for income and diversification (UBS House View - Daily US)
key_insights: US bond and equity markets stayed volatile as investors weighed mixed AI signals (TSMC gave a more cautious outlook) and further evidence of persistent US inflation.

September US PPI rose 1.3% on the month, the largest monthly increase in four and a half years, against a 0.5% consensus forecast. Energy drove much of it, but prices also rose across a broader range of goods and services.
The 10-year Treasury yield traded around 5.09%, close to its lowest level in three weeks, as equity volatility raised demand for high-quality bonds. UBS keeps fixed income at Attractive.

UBS expects the Fed to raise rates by another 50 basis points over the next 12 months, with increases in December and March and no change through late 2027. Market pricing is for nearly 90 basis points more, which UBS calls too hawkish.

Vice Chair Jefferson sees no immediate urgency to hike again, NY Fed President Williams sees no need for further increases in 2027, and SF Fed President Daly signals little urgency. UBS reads this as supporting a gradual path and lower Treasury yields.
Starting yields give an income cushion. 2-, 5- and 10-year Treasury yields would need to rise about 257, 113 and 65 basis points respectively for capital losses to offset the income earned.
A conventional 60/40 portfolio had a maximum recovery period of 4.2 years from bear market drawdowns since 1945, against 6.2 years for an all-equity portfolio.

Income-focused investors may use short-maturity bonds to limit duration risk. Investors who tolerate volatility may consider medium- to long-duration high-quality bonds. UBS stays cautious on the longest maturities because of fiscal concerns and rising AI-related issuance.
Odds of a Fed hike at the 27-28 October meeting fell below 15% from about 27% after Chair Warsh avoided signaling an imminent move. S&P 500 futures pointed to a 0.2% rise and the dollar weakened.

The Fed raised rates 25 basis points in September, its first hike since 2023. A majority of policymakers indicated another move would likely be appropriate this year, and Warsh declined to prejudge the remaining meetings.
Ukraine struck the Ryazan refinery (nearly 5% of Russian refinery throughput) after Zelenskyy said Kyiv was done supporting the energy-target ceasefire announced by Trump.

Iran and its proxies have carried out at least 135 drone and missile attacks on at least 84 infrastructure sites since late February, per a Reuters investigation. Targets included Fujairah, Ras Laffan and Saudi Arabia's East-West Pipeline.
US crude inventories fell 8.6 million barrels last week against an expected 288,000-barrel decline, after a hurricane shut in as much as 71.5% of Gulf of Mexico oil output.
UBS recently raised its year-end Brent forecast to USD 100 a barrel and favors actively managed, diversified commodity exposure across energy, precious metals, industrial metals and agriculture.

sector_views.rationale: Rated Attractive on elevated starting yields, income cushion, diversification, and scope for capital gains if Fed tightening expectations are scaled back.
Tight supply and durable demand support a commodity upcycle, with a preference for actively managed diversified exposure.
Resilient growth and robust earnings should help equities withstand moderately higher interest rates.

trade_ideas.rationale: Elevated starting yields give an income cushion, and yields should fall as markets scale back Fed tightening expectations.
trade_ideas.risk: Further yield volatility from elevated inflation, heavy debt supply and fiscal concerns. Cautious on the longest maturities.

trade_ideas.description: Actively managed, diversified commodity exposure across energy, precious metals, industrial metals and agriculture
trade_ideas.rationale: Tight supply and durable demand support a commodity upcycle.

risk_factors: Persistent US inflation, with September PPI broadening beyond energy.
Heavy debt supply, fiscal concerns and rising AI-related issuance pressuring long-maturity yields.
Mixed AI outlook signals, including TSMC's more cautious outlook.
Breakdown of the energy ceasefire and attacks on Russian and Persian Gulf energy infrastructure.
Strait of Hormuz and Red Sea traffic disruption.
Hurricane-related outages amplifying tight oil inventories, with emergency reserve releases offering only temporary relief.
vol_and_positioning: Equity market volatility increased risk aversion and supported demand for high-quality bonds.

tension_points.bull_case: UBS expects only 50 basis points more of Fed hikes (December and March), with Fed officials Jefferson, Williams and Daly signaling little urgency, so Treasury yields should fall and bonds gain.
tension_points.bear_case: September PPI (+1.3% m/m) and CPI came in above expectations with pressures broadening beyond energy, and market pricing is for nearly 90 basis points more tightening.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A majority of policymakers indicated another hike would likely be appropriate this year, and inflation persistence beyond energy could force faster tightening than UBS's December and March path.
